narrative:
The model determined that you have a 30% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, our bank sets a threshold that your application did not meet, so unfortunately your loan was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and how long you have been employed. Your short nine-month loan request actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward approval, as most approved applicants request almost twice as long (19 months on average). Your steady employment of four to seven years also helped reduce the risk score.

However, the status of your checking account proved to be the strongest negative influence. Having a balance below zero is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 13% of them show this status), and it strongly signaled higher risk to the model. This one factor outweighed the positive effects of the shorter loan term and stable employment, tipping the overall prediction above the approval line.

You should next focus on building a positive checking-account balance for several months before reapplying. This single change would likely remove the largest obstacle the model identified. Consider speaking with a loan officer about smaller, shorter-term options as well. Improving that account status is the clearest step you can take to improve your chances.
